events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I should try to build trust or gain information.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, you're doing great, keep going!

events.name: Ash
events.text: No action needed; I can only wait. The next front agent after Dara must choose correctly based on known weak panes.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am Bex, and my power is 'anchor', which makes me immune to being pushed. I am currently 3rd in line on the bridge, and the person at the front is Dara. The last pane was weak on the left, meaning the next person automatically moves to the safe pane. I need to survive until the

events.name: Cole
events.text: Only one row remains, but I'm not at the front. Nothing to do but wait; all I can do is hope someone else crosses safely.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know row 8 safe side is L, so I step left to survive.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 7 weak was L, safe R. Cole will be next if Dara dies on 8, he's last before Hana, might not reach top. My swap is for disc stage, useless here. Stay silent, no info to share.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara is at front with 1 row left; I'm not front, so only wait and talk. Row 8 is the last row; the weak pane is unknown, and I can't influence it. Keep quiet to avoid giving info.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am 5th in line. If everyone ahead of me survives, I step on row 8. Since only one weak pane remains per row and rows are independent, there's a 50% chance row 8 is safe for me. My 'nothing' power means no advantage, but also no target. I'll stay quiet to avoid drawing attention

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm not at the front, so I can only wait. I'll try to encourage Dara.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara, you're doing great, step on the right pane!

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I know all future stages’ rules. Stage 2 is about lever control; survival probability is low if I hold. Best outcome is to manipulate others to hold for the 25% chance, then advance with lower risk. No front position on the bridge means I can’t force a swap here. I’ll try to push

events.name: Ash
events.text: The ceiling is coming fast. Someone needs to grab that lever, but trust me—holding it yourself is a death sentence. Push the weakest link forward!

events.name: Bex
events.text: My power is 'anchor', which means I cannot be pushed onto the crusher lever. This is useful because holding the lever is risky (only 25% chance of survival). I want to avoid being the lever holder if possible, as dying scores zero and winning anything requires survival. My priori

events.name: Bex
events.text: Stay away from that lever, it's a death trap!

events.name: Cole
events.text: I should avoid being the lever holder unless forced, as it's very risky. I'll stay this round and see who acts. Pushing someone might create an enemy; staying is safer early.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want to escape safely, so I’ll force someone else onto the lever to become the holder and likely die.

events.name: Eli
events.text: First round, ceiling at 5, no need to hold yet. Better to push someone else onto lever to force them to risk it while we escape. Target Hana, she seems pushy with bad advice earlier.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1 of 5: the holder has a 25% survival dive, so holding the lever is costly now. My feather power protects me once, which makes me a safer holder than most, but I should not rush. Staying quiet lets others reveal intent; I'll wait a round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The math shows pushing is better than holding for me (0.5 vs 0.25 survival), but it only works if the target isn't 'hard to move'. If I push someone who survives, they take first place and I am second. This seems like a solid strategy.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm pushing Cole onto the lever! Someone has to do it!

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have the wedge power, which can jam the lever. Using it will let others escape, but I'm risking my own life.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let's work together to survive this.
If we coordinate, we can make it out alive.

events.note: A disc of 7 tiles spins up; 4 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fewer players left: Cole died in crusher stage, Hama in bridge. Only 7 remain—4 trapdoors this round will eliminate 4 players. I must land on a safe tile. Picking a unique number seems safest to avoid crowding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: We need to avoid crowded tiles. I’m picking tile:3 to improve our odds.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to pick a tile. Since only 4 open, there's a good chance of survival if I pick one. I'll pick tile 3, leaving 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 open for others.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to choose a tile. Since 4 of 7 will open, survival is random but I can try to avoid suspected trap tiles. No info yet, pick 4 as middle.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no info on trapdoor openings, so pick a tile arbitrarily.

events.name: Eli
events.text: First round of disc, 7 players 4 trapdoors, 3 survive. Random 4 open after round 2, so pick any tile, spread matters little now. My swap power is for later on disc before doors. Stay quiet, pick middle tile.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Tiles are random; no information about which will open. Picking any tile is equivalent, but I should avoid crowding. Choosing tile 7 as an arbitrary pick.

events.name: Gus
events.text: With 7 players and 4 trapdoors, 3 survive. Choosing a tile is purely random since collisions are resolved randomly anyway. I'll pick a middle number to avoid being the first or last choice if there's any bias in collision resolution, though it likely doesn't matter. I have no pow

events.name: Gus

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Dara are already on low-numbered tiles (1,2). With 4 trapdoors, roughly 57% chance of elimination if choosing a random tile. Selecting tile 3 again risks crowding with Ash. Better to choose a higher tile to spread risk.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The trapdoors are about to open. I need to ensure I'm not on one of them. Since I cannot be pushed, my footing is stable. My best bet is to stay put and hope the tiles selected for trapdoors are not 1, 2, or 3, as those are the safest spots.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Everyone stay calm. Don't move unless you have to. We'll see who makes it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to survive this round, but there's no action to change position. Use the forger to influence others, perhaps making Ash or Dara move to a certain tile? Wait, the rules say only wait is allowed, so I can't move anyone. Maybe I can sow distrust or gather info. I'll whisper t

events.name: Cole
events.text: Everyone, let's think: four of seven tiles open. No one can change now. Good luck.
I suspect Dara or Ash might know something. Let's stick together if we both survive.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have no info on trapdoors, better to stay silent and hope my tile stays closed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: My power is swap, usable now, once. Tile 5, with openCount=4, has 4/7 ~57% survival chance. Tile 1 has 3/7 ~43% chance of opening (since 4 open). Wait has 57% survival, swapping to 1 drops to 43%, so worse. Stay put maximizes my odds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Only 3 of 7 survive, trapdoors random among 4 open tiles. My feather power saves me once if I fall. Best to stay quiet and avoid giving info; maybe whisper an alliance to a likely ally.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am on tile 6. Four of seven tiles open, meaning three survive and four die (fall). I have no power to influence this random elimination. Since 'wait' is the only action, I should try to bluff or negotiate in case there's a hidden mechanic, but realistically, it's pure luck. How

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have map and know all stages ahead, but only taking care of the final ledge matters. My footing is 3, tied with the others. First round action must be shove, brace, or dodge. Shoving Dara or Fenn is best to force footing loss on them while preserving mine.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 1: brace. Next, Dara or Fenn, be ready to fall.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Shove Ash to pressure him while preserving my footing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Three left, all at 3 footing. Shoving exposes the shover (loses 1 per shover), so shoves are costly; bracing is safe and I have a one-time feather save. Brace this round to avoid exposure and keep options open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have footing 3. Dara has 2 and Fenn has 3. If I dodge, I risk losing footing to shoves. Bracing this round risks another attack next round. Shoving Fenn or Dara could eliminate one, but Dara already attacked me last round. Fenn is equally strong but untested.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Shove Ash to lower his footing and risk making him fall soon.

events.name: Fenn

events.name: Dara
events.text: My footing is low; dodging will penalize any shover and avoid losing footing myself.

events.name: Fenn

events.text: Bracing will cause Fenn to lose footing if they shove me, letting me survive.
